title: Session, token, cookie, key material
status: AUTHORED. The state that survives between requests, and the one most often carried in the wrong place.

atom_notes.A03: a session is an identity claim, so session bugs are identity bugs
atom_notes.A04: rotation, fixation and revocation are all questions about state agreement
atom_notes.A09: token crypto and cookie integrity are the same class as any other signature
atom_notes.A08: storage and cookie attributes leak what the app thought was private

required_cells.why: find where the session actually lives before testing it
attribute and rotation testing needs replay control
fixation or forgery is the exploitation step
a token that decrypts is not a token that is accepted
rotation and revocation drift over time

tree.q: Where does the session state actually live?
tree.why: Cookie, localStorage, bearer token, or a server side store. Each has a different failure mode and most people assume the cookie without checking.

branches.action: read the attributes, then test rotation on login, logout, and privilege change
branches.oracle: the same id used after rotation

branches.action: check what the client can read and what an XSS would get. then check server side validation of that value
branches.oracle: server accepts a client modified value

branches.action: decode, then test validation: algorithm, audience, expiry, revocation
branches.oracle: server accepts a token it should reject

branches.action: test idle and absolute timeout, concurrent sessions, and revocation on password change
branches.oracle: session still valid after the event that should end it

gaps.gap: No tool that reports where session state lives across the whole app

gaps.gap: No revocation tester that measures the window between logout and token expiry
gaps.build_candidate: loop replay after revocation, record the window in seconds
